about: The Hyperion set (engine/docs/replay-test.md): games 1.17 cannot play, each recorded by replaytest.py hxrecord with Hyperion's --record on a map of testrun/play/maps/Hyperion (remade by tools/hxmap/remake.py, kept local), the local player idle, or giving orders every `orders` frames (--record-orders), and the other slots computers. A game ends at its frames, or sooner when the local player has lost. An entry with a checkpoint is saved at that frame, and the save kept beside its replay.

games.name: h16_bgh2x_save
games.about: h16_bgh2x saved at its checkpoint: the replay makes the save again, and the save loaded goes on as the live game did

games.name: h16_goa2x_end
games.about: played until the idle local player has lost, through melee defeat and victory, which walk the foes and all players groups

games.about: h64_bgh4x4 saved at its checkpoint

games.name: h64_bgh8x8
games.about: 64 players on Big Game Hunters tiled 8 by 8 (1,024 tiles a side, 32,768 pixels), the bases of other starts kept up to 12,000 units: positions of 31 bits (stage E4), the minimap at 8:1

games.name: h4_lt_rules
games.about: a map 1.17 plays, played by Hyperion's rules (--rules hyperion): its replay and save are Hyperion's and name the rules; the map is copied from the 1.17 install into testrun/play/maps/classic/

games.name: h16_xl1800_queue
games.about: queued commands (--record-orders 24,queue): the local player's armies take their moves and right-clicks queued, up to the 8 a queue holds, while the order limit of HX_OPT_ORDER_QUEUE is in force, as every new game by Hyperion's rules records it; the replay and the save go on as the live game did. In this game the orders the game itself gives meet a queue only as a worker's UndoTransparentWorker re-issues itself, about 4,000 times, which the limit lets through

games.name: h2_wide_select
games.about: Hyperion's selection (HX_OPT_SELECTION) on the wide selection test map (tools/hxmap/widemap.py): the local player selects its 200 zerglings and its buildings, up to 255 units sent in chunks of 0x8C; its three Gateways train together, each Zealot going to the one with the shortest queue; and a control group is made of the selection and called back (port_record.cpp, WideRound). Saved at its checkpoint with every human's selection and groups in HXST

games.name: h3_hybrid
games.about: a game with a mod's types: the hybrid-test mod's Hybrid Reavers, placed by the map (tools/hxmap/hybridmap.py), sent by the local player's orders at zerglings and marines, one casting every fifth round of orders, Psionic Shockwave and Psionic Lance (aimed at the round's target) by turns, the Lance once the Templar Archives the orders send to research it has done so (frame 2,571), while the Forge upgrades Hybrid Claws (level 2 by frame 2,900); its replay and save name the mod and its data's fingerprint and play back or load only with it (--mod hybrid-test)

games.name: h3_wide
games.about: h3_hybrid's game with the wide-test mod: the Hybrid Test's rows behind rows of padding, so that its techs and upgrade are 256 and on, its orders 260, its weapons 260, its flingy 268, its sprite 1,100 and its images 2,100, with 300 more unit types after the Hybrid Reaver. The research, the upgrade and the casts go out as the wide commands (0x97, 0x98, 0x96); the save holds the high bytes (HXWI) and the mod's techs and upgrades (HXMT), and both go on as the live game did

games.name: h5_lt_hybrid_race
games.about: a mod's race: the local player plays the hybrid-test mod's Hybrid race on a melee map against a computer, starting with its own start units and its Gateway's card without the Dark Templar; its replay and save name each slot's race (RACE, HXRA)

games.name: h6_lt_hybrid_computer
games.about: a computer of a mod's race: the hybrid-test mod's Hybrid race against an idle local player, seated as Protoss (--computer-race hybrid) and given the race at its slot after the start positions; it plays 1.17's Protoss scripts, making a Hybrid Reaver where they ask for Dark Templar (the race's ai): it opens with Zealots, has 18 by its save at 9,500, and played on destroys the idle player by frame 10,573

games.name: h64_bgh8x8_orders
games.about: the 1,024-tile map with the local player giving orders every 24 frames, saved at its checkpoint

games.name: h16_bgh2x_levels
games.about: every computer level (port_ai.h) in one game, saved at its checkpoint: the replay and the save hold each slot's level (AILV, HXAI), and both go on as the live game did

games.name: h4_lt_handicap
games.about: handicaps (HX_OPT_HANDICAP): the local player at 50% and its three computers at 60, 80 and 100%, each unit's maximum life and shields at its owner's share as it is made, builds, heals and regenerates; the local player's orders send its units into the computers', which beat it soon after this game's last frame. Seed 405 because on others (402 to 406) the replay's creep tiles or thingies drew other cosmetic random numbers than the live game's, with or without handicaps (the tracker's bug of 2026-10-23); the games agree in every other part to the last frame. The replay and the save hold each slot's handicap (HCAP, HXHC), and both go on as the live game did

games.name: h4_lt_mutators
games.about: mutators (HX_OPT_MUTATORS), the resource and supply ones at once: mineral fields at half, geysers that never run dry, 1,000 minerals and 500 gas and 8 workers to start, a supply cap of 300 and half as much supply again from each supplier; the Terran player and its three Protoss computers build, mine and grow by them. Protoss computers, so that no creep spreads: a zerg base's creep tiles are pictures drawn from the C runtime's rand, which a live game and its replay draw differently (the tracker's creep tiles bug), and under these mutators the zerg's creep reaches new tiles by frame 2592. The replay and the save hold the set (MUTS, HXMU), and both go on as the live game did

games.name: h4_lt_mutators_later
games.about: the fog, build time and tech mutators (HX_OPT_MUTATORS) at once: no fog of war, so every player sees the whole map all game; buildings, units, research and upgrades in half their time; and every ability researched and every upgrade at its top level from the start. The Terran player and three Protoss computers (no creep, as h4_lt_mutators). The times and the tech are the game's own tables, set as the map loads, and the fog is kept open after each sight refresh; the replay and the save hold the set, and the save keeps the tables and the fog, so both go on as the live game did

games.name: h4_lt_rich
games.about: rich bases (HX_OPT_MUTATORS): the bases past the naturals that the read finds fair turn rich on a roll of the game's seed, their mineral fields giving 11 a trip and their geysers 16; the Terran player and three Protoss computers (no creep, as h4_lt_mutators) mine them. The replay holds the set and the list of rich resources (MUTS, RICH), so it plays the list back rather than rolling again, and the save keeps each unit's flag and each worker's rich load (HXST), so both go on as the live game did
